chapters.name: Signs, Signals, and Pavement Markings
chapters.summary: What sign shapes and colors mean, how to respond to steady and flashing traffic lights and arrows, and what lane lines and other pavement markings tell you.
keyPoints: An eight-sided red sign means stop. A downward-pointing triangle means yield.
Yellow diamond signs warn of hazards ahead. Orange signs mark work zones.
A flashing red light means stop completely, then go when it is safe. A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.
A solid yellow line on your side of the center means you may not pass.

chapters.name: Right of Way and Turns
chapters.summary: Who goes first at intersections, four-way stops, and roundabouts, how to turn correctly, and when you must yield to pedestrians and emergency vehicles.
keyPoints: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to stop goes first. If two arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.
Inside a roundabout, traffic moves counterclockwise, and entering drivers yield to traffic already in the circle.

chapters.name: Speed, Passing, and Parking
chapters.summary: Florida speed limits, choosing a safe speed, signaling, lane use and passing, and where you may not park.
keyPoints: Unless signs say otherwise, the speed limit is 30 mph in business or residential areas and 55 mph on other roads.
Signal at least 100 feet before you turn.
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

chapters.name: Safe Driving and Sharing the Road
chapters.summary: Driving at night and in bad weather, handling emergencies, and sharing the road with school buses, emergency and service vehicles, trucks, motorcycles, bicycles, pedestrians, and trains.
keyPoints: Use headlights from sunset to sunrise and when rain, smoke, or fog makes it hard to see. Dim high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
Stop for a school bus with its stop signal out unless it is on the other side of a divided highway with a raised barrier or an unpaved median at least 5 feet wide.
Under the Move Over law, change lanes away from a stopped emergency or service vehicle, or slow to 20 mph below the posted limit if you cannot.

chapters.name: Licensing, Alcohol, and Driver Responsibility
chapters.summary: Learner and teen driver rules, seat belts and child seats, phones and texting, alcohol and drug laws, insurance, and what to do after a crash.
keyPoints: It is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol level of 0.08% or more. For drivers under 21, the limit is 0.02%.
Refusing a lawful breath, blood, or urine test the first time leads to a one-year license suspension.
A learner license holder must drive with a licensed driver age 21 or older in the front passenger seat.
